raw_response:
I’m 63 now, and I don’t like taking big risks. This land is only 16.1 mu, and I farm it mostly by myself, so I do what has worked steady in the village. Wheat and maize together is still the safest for me. Wheat gives me the main grain, then maize goes in right after harvest. I have a well, so if the sky stays dry I can still manage, but pumping water costs money, so I won’t water too many times unless the crop really needs it.

For wheat, I’ll use a local improved variety like most people here use, sow in early October, and put the base fertilizer on before sowing. I usually don’t dare cut fertilizer too much, because if wheat turns yellow later the yield drops fast. But I also can’t spend too much at once, so I split it: some at sowing, some at jointing. I’ll water around the key times if rain is short. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll get maize in quickly, same field, no delay. That turnaround is always tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and use machine help if needed. For maize I’ll use hybrid seed, one base fertilizer dose and one topdress around knee-high stage if the plants look decent and I still have cash. I farm alone, so I try to keep labor-saving methods and not make the plan too fancy. What I want is stable harvest, not chasing the very highest yield.
